items.summary: The `design` enforcement_level is overloaded: in ckeletin-rust's report it labels both structurally-strong enforcement (CKSPEC-ARCH-007 — a stray root .rs file belongs to no crate and is not built, effectively compile-time) and near-attestation (CKSPEC-CL-004, ENF-003, ENF-004 — 'documented in the CONFORMANCE.md audit table'). One label thus spans the strongest and weakest ends of the ladder and no longer communicates enforcement strength. Surfaced when enforcement_level validation was first added (it was previously unvalidated, so `design`/`test` shipped unchecked).
items.rationale: Proposed resolution to discuss with the consumer: introduce a distinct `structural` level for the un-buildable cases and route documentation/attestation cases to `honor-system`, then have ckeletin-rust reclassify its 6 `design` entries. Held at `discuss` rather than `update` because the conformance/*.yaml aggregates are regenerated from ckeletin-rust's published data, so the implementation gets a vote before the enum changes; adding `structural` to the schema before any consumer uses it would be decorative vocabulary.
